body: {"status":"ok","message-type":"work-list","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"facets":{},"total-results":1295818,"items":[{"abstract":"<jats:p>Replay-free class-incremental vibration diagnosis must incorporate new fault categories after deployment while retaining earlier decisions without storing old signals. Sequential optimization is difficult in this setting because it can distort both individual class representatives and their relative geometry, especially when vibration patterns also vary with operating conditions. We introduce graph continual prototype learning (GCPL), which represents each observed class by a prototype and connects related prototypes through a sparse feature-space graph. New-class samples initialize new nodes and local edges, whereas node- and edge-stability terms constrain changes to the previously learned class structure. The graph is learned from embeddings rather than predefined fault taxonomies, and its retained state scales with the number of classes instead of the number of vibration windows. A leakage-resistant evaluation protocol is specified for four public bearing datasets and jointly measures cumulative-class accuracy, old-class forgetting, new-class learning, and robustness to operating-condition shifts. This formulation provides a compact pattern-recognition framework for studying relational structure in replay-free incremental diagnosis.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.2139\/ssrn.7230759","type":"posted-content","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Graph continual prototype learning for replay-free class-incremental vibration diagnosis"],"author":[{"given":"qinao","family":"hu","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026]]},"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.2139\/ssrn.7230759"},{"abstract":"<jats:p>Intelligent condition-monitoring systems must often incorporate fault categories that appear after deployment, while retaining historical vibration records may be restricted by storage, privacy, or maintenance constraints. This paper addresses the resulting replay-free class-incremental vibration fault diagnosis problem. We propose graph continual prototype learning (GCPL), a compact AI-based diagnostic framework that stores class prototypes, diagonal dispersion estimates, and a sparse relation graph instead of previous signal windows. New classes are inserted locally, while prototype anchoring, old-edge consistency, neighborhood-rank preservation, reliability weighting, and a topology-aware boundary margin constrain destabilization of the retained class structure. Record- or bearing-level splits are applied before windowing on CWRU, Paderborn, XJTU-SY, and JNU to avoid overlapping-window leakage. Across four datasets and five matched seeds, GCPL attains AIA values of 95.1%, 91.2%, 89.5%, and 92.4%, improving on the strongest replay-free baseline by 2.1\u20132.6 points and reducing final-session forgetting by 1.8\u20132.3 points. Additional tests cover relation drift, operating-condition shift, additive noise, low-shot and long-tail increments, class order, calibration, and retained-state efficiency. The results indicate that preserving inter-class topology is an effective compact memory mechanism for adaptive vibration monitoring.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.2139\/ssrn.7315097","type":"posted-content","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Relation-preserving graph continual prototype learning for replay-free class-incremental vibration fault diagnosis"],"author":[{"given":"qinao","family":"hu","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2026]]},"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.2139\/ssrn.7315097"},{"abstract":"<jats:p>Background: Continual learning (CL) is increasingly important for developing adaptive clinical AI models; however, its application to histopathology remains challenging due to privacy constraints, expanding diagnostic categories, and staining variability. We investigate CL for histopathology image classification under a class-incremental learning (CIL) scenario, where new diagnostic categories are introduced sequentially. Methods: We benchmark representative regularization-, replay-, architecture-, and prompt-based CL methods on the NCT-CRC-HE-100K dataset, with additional validation on CRC-HE-7K. We compare four normalization strategies and analyze the effects of replay buffer size and training epochs. In addition to average accuracy and forgetting, we conduct clinical relevance and error analysis using confusion matrices, ROC curves, and misclassification cases, then assess training dynamics and computational efficiency. Results: Dataset-level normalization consistently achieves the best performance among the evaluated normalization strategies. Among replay-based methods, DER++ achieves strong performance when previous-task images can be stored and replayed, reaching an average accuracy of 94.77\u00b11.82 and forgetting of 3.66\u00b11.73 with a buffer size of 500 and 50 training epochs. However, it requires higher memory usage, longer training time, and storage of previous samples. Among prompt-based methods, DualPrompt performs best with 5 epochs, reaching an average accuracy of 88.97\u00b10.60 and forgetting of 7.70\u00b11.21 while showing smoother training behavior and lower computational cost. Conclusions: Replay-based methods achieve higher accuracy and lower forgetting when exemplar storage and sufficient computational resources are available, but introduce higher computational and privacy costs. Prompt-based methods provide a competitive exemplar-free alternative under privacy- and resource-constrained settings. Dataset-level normalization is also important for stable CL performance in histopathology
